A1.justification: Despite the new AVEX title and conference formatting, both PDFs describe the same bioacoustic encoder study. Their main texts, tables, figures, equations and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original encoder-training experiments, benchmark evaluations and data-mixture ablations in Sections 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds BirdMAE evaluations and supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The proposed EfficientNet, BEATs and EAT encoder architectures, objectives, augmentations and training recipes remain unchanged. Appendix C.6 introduces attention probing as an alternative downstream evaluation procedure, without revising the proposed encoders.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluation task coverage are retained. ESC-50 already appears in v1 Table 8; v3's analysis excluding it is a sensitivity analysis of existing results. Direct BirdSet evaluation and attention probing reuse existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Bird-MAE-Huge is added to the aggregate comparison and all four detailed result tables in v3 Tables 3 and 6–9. BirdMAE was previously discussed but not evaluated. All existing comparison models remain.

E3.justification: v3 adds BirdSet LT+ evaluation using post-trained classifier logits instead of dataset-specific probing. A separate linear-versus-attention comparison uses matched 50-epoch training and cosine scheduling. These supplement the retained main evaluation protocols rather than replacing them.

E4.justification: Appendix C.4–C.6 substantially expands sensitivity analysis: excluding ESC-50 tests benchmark-composition effects, LT+ versus DT tests downstream adaptation choices, and attention versus linear probing tests dependence on the evaluation head. The earlier data-mixture and taxonomic ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose fixed seed 42 and lack repeated-seed uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added win-rate equations explain existing aggregation rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: All matched table scores for the original 19 models remain unchanged. v3 adds BirdMAE results and substantial supplementary findings in Tables 10–11 and Figure 7. For example, the new 50-epoch comparison reports pretrained BEATs at 0.44 versus 0.27 BEANS Detection mAP with attention versus linear probing, changing model rankings under that protocol.

T1.justification: The accuracy, average-precision, AUC and NMI definitions are retained. Appendix B.3 adds standard formulas explaining relative gains and win rates already reported in v1; it introduces no substantive theoretical result, proof or revised mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central claims about diverse training audio and sequential self-supervised/supervised training remain. The abstract expands the resource contribution from a promised checkpoint release to reported released checkpoints and the AVEX inference, training and evaluation library.

C2.justification: v3 acknowledges uncontrolled species/noise confounds in Section 4.2, qualifies general-audio benefits after excluding ESC-50, and adds explanations involving overfitting and temporal representations. Conversely, v1's conclusion paragraph on Northern Hemisphere bias and uncertain generalization to underrepresented taxa is removed.

D1.justification: v3 reports released checkpoints and an AVEX library with project and repository access information, replacing v1's future-release promise. It newly documents the original 900-epoch probing hyperparameters, parameter-selection rationale and win-rate calculations. However, v1 Table 3's per-dataset label counts and source catalog are omitted.

R1.justification: Most research positioning is retained. v3 removes the introduction's explicit contrast with Ghani et al. (2025) and Kather et al. (2025), drops the Ghani reference, and removes several dataset-source references associated with the deleted evaluation catalog. BirdMAE was already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence remain recognizable. Changes include the AVEX title, author-contribution labels, topical subheadings in related work and evaluation, retitled results sections, and reorganized appendix explanations.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR layout, consolidates v1 Tables 5–6 into a shaded aggregate table, moves the research-comparison table to Appendix A, and removes the detailed evaluation-dataset table. It also adds Tables 10–11 and Figures 6–7, updates Figure 2, and substantially rearranges figure placement.

improvement.justification: The added benchmark-composition and probing checks better qualify the empirical conclusions, while BirdMAE evaluation and the reported AVEX release improve comparison and reuse. These gains are partly offset by losing the detailed dataset-label catalog and geographic/underrepresented-taxa limitation. The evidence supports a modest net improvement.
